newsitem.title: FRANCE: Unsettled weather in French grain, sugar areas.
newsitem.headline: Unsettled weather in French grain, sugar areas.

text.p: Unsettled weather continued across most of the French grain and sugar belts on Wednesday, but showers were becoming more scattered and accompanied by strong winds, weather office Meteo France said.
Moderate showers fell across parts of the southwest, where steady rain earlier this week allowed farmers to resume maize sowings delayed by weeks of drought.
Light snow fell at the southern tip of the Paris grain basin near Tours.
Meteo France said showers were darting quickly eastwards, with storms in many areas and gusts up to 80 km per hour in the northwest.
Maximum temperatures were below normal for the time of year at 6-10 degrees Celsius in northern France and 10-16 degrees in the south.
Independent U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp reiterated predictions for significant drought-breaking rain in western European wheat areas this week.
"Current weather is more favourably mild in the southeast where past cold temperatures caused problems," it said.
